query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve dynamic strength–ductility performance? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an untreated baseline, defines the boundary conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Grain refinement through hot rolling can improve the dynamic strength-ductility performance of high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast high-entropy alloy with a single body-centered cubic structure
generation.structural_mediator: Refined grain size, increased grain boundary area
generation.mechanism: Grain boundary strengthening, solid solution strengthening, and dynamic recrystallization
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved yield strength and ductility, with a potential increase in yield strength of up to 20% and ductility of up to 15%
generation.baseline: As-cast high-entropy alloy without hot rolling
generation.boundary: High-entropy alloys with a single body-centered cubic structure, grain size refinement through hot rolling
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of grain refinement and its effect on dynamic strength-ductility performance may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the dynamic strength-ductility performance of as-cast and hot-rolled high-entropy alloys with a single body-centered cubic structure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the hot-rolled alloy does not exhibit improved yield strength and ductility compared to the as-cast alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

Evidence of Inverse Hall-Petch Behavior and Low Friction and Wear in High Entropy Alloys

Abstract: AbstractWe present evidence of inverse Hall-Petch behavior for a single-phase high entropy alloy (CoCrFeMnNi) in ultra-high vacuum and show that it is associated with low friction coefficients (~0.3). Grain size measurements by STEM validate a recently proposed dynamic amorphization model that accurately predicts grain size-dependent shear strength in the inverse Hall-Petch regime. Wear rates in the initially soft (coarse grained) material were shown to be remarkably low (~10–6 mm3/N-m), the lowest for any HEA tested in an inert environment where oxidation and the formation of mixed metal-oxide films is mitigated. The combined high wear resistance and low friction are linked to the formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer. The dynamic amorphization model was also used to predict an average high angle grain boundary energy (0.87 J/m2). This value was used to explain cavitation-induced nanoporosity found in the highly deformed surface layer, a phenomenon that has been linked to superplasticity.Subject terms: Structural materials, Structural properties

Hierarchical microstructure strengthening in a single crystal high entropy superalloy

Abstract: AbstractA hierarchical microstructure strengthened high entropy superalloy (HESA) with superior cost specific yield strength from room temperature up to 1,023 K is presented. By phase transformation pathway through metastability, HESA possesses a hierarchical microstructure containing a dispersion of nano size disordered FCC particles inside ordered L12 precipitates that are within the FCC matrix. The average tensile yield strength of HESA from room temperature to 1,023 K could be 120 MPa higher than that of advanced single crystal superalloy, while HESA could still exhibit an elongation greater than 20%. Furthermore, the cost specific yield strength of HESA can be 8 times that of some superalloys. A template for lighter, stronger, cheaper, and more ductile high temperature alloy is proposed.Subject terms: Mechanical properties, Metals and alloys

Remarkable Enhanced Mechanical Properties of TiAlCrNbV Medium-Entropy Alloy with Zr Additions

Abstract: Most medium entropy alloys (MEAs) exhibit excellent mechanical properties, but their applications are limited because of their high density. This study explores a series of lightweight nonequiatomic Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx (x = 3, 5, 7, and 10) MEAs with a low density, high strength, and high ductility. To achieve solid solution strengthening, Zr with a large atomic radius was used. In addition, various thermomechanical treatment parameters were adopted to further improve the MEAs’ mechanical properties. The density of the MEAs was revealed to be approximately 5 g/cm3, indicating that they were lightweight. Through an X-ray diffraction analysis, the MEAs were revealed to have a single body-centered cubic structure not only in the as-cast state but also after thermomechanical treatment. In terms of mechanical properties, all the as-cast MEAs with Zr additions achieved excellent performance (>1000 MPa tensile yield strength and 20% tensile ductility).
